ToastTab CHN._comment: Chennai. Derived from a 7-day SERVICE HISTORY (Wed 01 Jul – Thu 09 Jul 2026, weekdays only), not a written rulebook — see docs/chennai_client_logic.md for the grid and how each rule was read off it. THE ONE ASSUMPTION: the sample spans two part-weeks whose weekday→theme mapping conflicts (Wed is south on 01 Jul but biryani on 08 Jul; Thu is north on 02 Jul but south on 09 Jul), so the theme map is inferred from the later, more complete run 06–09 Jul — Mon/Thu/Fri south, Tue north, Wed biryani. That fits 5 of the 7 observed days and reproduces the sample's 4 south : 2 north : 1 biryani ratio scaled to a 5-day week. The weekday lists below FOLLOW from that map: if the real theme map differs, these lists must move with it, because what the sample actually determines is the THEME each slot belongs to, not the weekday.

rules._comment: White rice on the SOUTH days only. The sample is 7/7 on this: white rice appears on every south day and on no north or biryani day, where a flavoured rice takes its place — one rice per day, never two (the same structure Amadeus Pune has).
rules.name: toast_tab_chn_white_rice_south_days

rules._comment: Flavoured rice on the NORTH and BIRYANI days only — peas pulao (north), ghee bisibelebath (north), veg biryani (biryani) in the sample. Complement of the white-rice list, so exactly one rice fills every day.
rules.name: toast_tab_chn_flavour_rice_north_biryani_days

rules._comment: Rasam on the SOUTH days only — the 'RASAM / CURD' cell, which the source workbook auto-split into two servings. It appears on all four south days and none of the others: with no plain rice to eat it with, a north or biryani day serves curd rice instead.
rules.name: toast_tab_chn_rasam_south_days

rules._comment: The curd half of 'RASAM / CURD', same four south days. The biryani day's RAITHA is a curd_side too, which is why `wed` is included here but not in the rasam list — a biryani gets a raita, not a rasam.
rules.name: toast_tab_chn_curd_side_south_and_biryani_days

rules._comment: Curd rice on the NORTH and BIRYANI days — the sour/yogurt component when there is no white rice + rasam. 3/3 in the sample.
rules.name: toast_tab_chn_curd_rice_north_biryani_days

rules._comment: Overrides the city rule of the same name (merged by name, so this REPLACES chennai.json's max of 1). Chennai's cap of one maida bread a week is simply wrong for this client: the sample serves a maida bread on 4 of 7 days (aloo paratha, butter kulcha, kothu parotta, paratha) and only 3 of the 5 non-maida wheat breads in the whole 29-dish pool are chapati variants. Client-confirmed at 2 a week, replacing the 3 I had read off the sample (which serves a maida bread on 4 of 7 days). Feasible because only the maida DAYS are capped: the 5 non-maida wheat flatbreads include the chapati family, which plain_chapati_may_repeat exempts from uniqueness, so the remaining 3 days draw from a 5-dish pool. Without this the pre-flight gate correctly answered 422: the wheat-flatbread composition below forces a maida bread on days the cap forbids.
rules.name: maida_bread_weekly

rules._comment: The bread is always a wheat or maida flat bread, never the dosai/idly family. Every one of the seven sampled breads is chapati, paratha, kulcha or kothu parotta; Chennai's 29-dish bread pool also holds 9 rice-breads (dosai, idly, appam) and the solver picked 'podi idly' as a bread row until this was added. A one-slot composition component with count 1 IS 'this slot must be a matching dish' (note 20) — `fixed_daily_item` would be the wrong tool, it only makes the choice consistent.
rules.name: toast_tab_chn_bread_is_a_wheat_flatbread
